question: If AI tools make the most progress before anyone outside the lab can use them, how can the public keep up?
reflection: Open logs of how a result was found can turn private AI breakthroughs into lessons everyone can learn from.

sources.subject: Anthropic Claude jumps Riemann Hypothesis from 41% to 67% in history

one_line: Unreleased AI models are reportedly producing major results in math and security before the public can use them.

top_stories.title: Big step on a famous math problem
top_stories.what: An unreleased Claude model reportedly raised the proven share of a key set of values in a 160-year-old math problem from about 42 to 67 percent, using many helper agents.
top_stories.why: Large, logged agent teams may change how hard research problems are tackled in other fields.

top_stories.title: Security model for vetted defenders
top_stories.what: OpenAI split its security program into a general tier and a restricted tier with a model that reportedly found two unknown flaws in a major browser engine.
top_stories.why: Access limited to vetted users is becoming the model for releasing risky AI skills.

top_stories.title: Fast open model for agents
top_stories.what: NVIDIA released an open model that uses only a tenth of its parts at a time and reportedly runs four times faster than models of similar size.
top_stories.why: Faster small models make routine agent steps cheaper for research teams.

saudi_lens.text: Tiered access to cyber-capable models raises a question for Saudi defenders: how national security teams can qualify for the restricted tiers.

idea.title: AI agents versus A/B tests
idea.pitch: Following a reported test by a large retailer, compare simulated user agents with a real A/B test on a public service page.
idea.first_step: Pick one past A/B test with known results to use as the benchmark.

idea_kids.title: Many small helpers
idea_kids.pitch: A group puzzle where each child solves one small piece of a big picture, then the class puts the pieces together.
idea_kids.first_step: Cut a large drawing into 20 numbered pieces with a simple task on each.
